# dormr2

> Multiplies a general matrix by the orthogonal matrix from a RQ factorization determined by sgerqf (unblocked algorithm).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dormr2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dormr2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dormr2( order, side, trans, M, N, K, A, LDA, TAU, strideTAU, C, LDC, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `side` | `OperationSide` | `'left'`: apply Q or Q\*\*T from the Left `'right'`: apply Q or Q\*\*T from the Right. |
| `trans` | `"no-transpose" \| "transpose"` | `'no-transpose'`: apply Q (No transpose) `'transpose'`: apply Q' (Transpose) |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of rows of the matrix C.<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of columns of the matrix C.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of elementary reflectors whose product defines the matrix Q.<br>Rejects `K < 0 \|\| K > (side === 'left' ? M : N)` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>K × (side === 'left' ? M : N)</sub> | The i-th row must contain the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i), for i = 1,2,...,k, as returned by DGERQF in the last k rows of its array argument A. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, K)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, side === 'left' ? M : N)` |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length K</sub> | TAU(i) must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by DGERQF. |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride length for `TAU` |
| `C` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the m by n matrix C. On exit, C is overwritten by Q\*C or Q\*\*T\*C or C\*Q\*\*T or C\*Q. |
| ↳ `LDC` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `C`<br>Column-major requires `LDC ≥ max(1, M)`<br>Row-major requires `LDC ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `N` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'L'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Left
  -   `= 'R'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Right
- `trans`:

  -   `= 'N'`: apply Q  (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: apply Q' (Transpose)
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix C. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix C. $N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The number of elementary reflectors whose product defines the matrix Q. If `SIDE = 'L'`, $M \ge K \ge 0$; if `SIDE = 'R'`, $N \ge K \ge 0$.
- `A`: (`LDA`,N) if `SIDE = 'R'` The i-th row must contain the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i), for $i = 1$,2,...,k, as returned by DGERQF in the last k rows of its array argument A. A is modified by the routine but restored on exit.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by DGERQF.
- `C`: On entry, the m by n matrix C. On exit, C is overwritten by $Q \, C$ or $Q^T \, C$ or $C \, Q^T$ or $C \, Q$.
- `WORK`: (M) if `SIDE = 'R'`

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid operation side
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `K < 0 \|\| K > ( side === "left" ? M : N )`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, K )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, side === 'left' ? M : N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dormr2.strided(
    side, trans,
    M, N, K,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    C, strideC1, strideC2, offsetC,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

Overwrites the M-by-N matrix C with Q_C, Q^T_C, C_Q, or C_Q^T.
where Q is a real orthogonal matrix defined as the product of K
elementary reflectors Q = H(1) H(2) ... H(k) as returned by DGERQF.

The reflectors are stored in ROWS of A (rowwise storage from RQ factorization).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `side` | `OperationSide` | 'left' to apply Q from left, 'right' from right |
| `trans` | `"no-transpose" \| "transpose"` | 'no-transpose' for Q, 'transpose' for Q^T |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of C<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of C<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elementary reflectors<br>Rejects `K < 0 \|\| K > (side === 'left' ? M : N)` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>K × (side === 'left' ? M : N)</sub> | Reflector vectors from DGERQF (K rows) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length K</sub> | Scalar factors of reflectors |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride for TAU |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for TAU |
| `C` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix |
| ↳ `strideC1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of C |
| ↳ `strideC2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of C |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for C |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Workspace array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'L'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Left
  -   `= 'R'`: apply Q or $Q^T$ from the Right
- `trans`:

  -   `= 'N'`: apply Q  (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: apply Q' (Transpose)
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix C. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix C. $N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The number of elementary reflectors whose product defines the matrix Q. If `SIDE = 'L'`, $M \ge K \ge 0$; if `SIDE = 'R'`, $N \ge K \ge 0$.
- `A`: (`LDA`,N) if `SIDE = 'R'` The i-th row must contain the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i), for $i = 1$,2,...,k, as returned by DGERQF in the last k rows of its array argument A. A is modified by the routine but restored on exit.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by DGERQF.
- `C`: On entry, the m by n matrix C. On exit, C is overwritten by $Q \, C$ or $Q^T \, C$ or $C \, Q^T$ or $C \, Q$.
- `WORK`: (M) if `SIDE = 'R'`

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid operation side
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `K < 0 \|\| K > ( side === "left" ? M : N )`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `(M === 0 || N === 0) || K === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dormr2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dormr2';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const C = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const TAU = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dormr2( 'column-major', 'left', 'no-transpose', N, N, N, A, N, TAU, 1, C, N, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
out = dormr2.strided( 'left', 'no-transpose', N, N, N, A, N, 1, 0, TAU, 1, 0, C, N, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DORMR2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DORMR2 overwrites the general real m by n matrix C with

$$
Q \, C \quad\text{if}\quad \mathrm{SIDE} = \text{'L'} \quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'N'}, \quad\text{or}\quad
$$

$$
Q^T \, C \quad\text{if}\quad \mathrm{SIDE} = \text{'L'} \quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'T'}, \quad\text{or}\quad
$$

$$
C \, Q \quad\text{if}\quad \mathrm{SIDE} = \text{'R'} \quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'N'}, \quad\text{or}\quad
$$

$$
C \, Q^T \quad\text{if}\quad \mathrm{SIDE} = \text{'R'} \quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'T'}
$$

where Q is a real orthogonal matrix defined as the product of k elementary reflectors

$$
Q = H(1) H(2) \cdots H(k)
$$

as returned by DGERQF. Q is of order m if `SIDE = 'L'` and of order n if `SIDE = 'R'`.

</section>
